results.content:
The economy remains a top concern for Americans, too, with 36.5% of August respondents citing economic factors like inflation, jobs and taxes as the most important issue in the United States. The second- and third-place issues were threats to democracy (15.8%) and health care (15.5%). This reflects a notable rise, as in July only 27.1% of likely voters thought economic factors were the most important issue, while threats to democracy ranked first at 28.3%.
